slides.title:
Four of the worst outages
we've been called into
slides.body:
had *nothing* to do
with the network.

slides.title: What they shared
slides.body:
A change somebody made
without telling anyone
who'd have to *live with it*.

slides.title: One
slides.body:
A certificate update.
Correct. Tested.
Entirely within their remit.

slides.title: What broke
slides.body:
A monitoring system had been
*pinning* that certificate
for three years.

slides.title: Two
slides.body:
A patch field relabelled
during an office move.
Nothing electrical changed.

slides.title: What broke
slides.body:
The labels were the
*only map* anyone had.

slides.title: Three
slides.body:
Compression enabled on a
replication job.
To be *helpful*.

slides.title: What broke
slides.body:
The traffic shape changed.
The threshold was tuned
to the *old* one.

slides.title: The pattern
steps: Each change was reasonable inside the team that made it.

slides.title:
Processes prove a change
was *authorized*.
slides.body:
Few make sure
it was *announced*.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
